subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through this as a static hover vehicle rather than a jointed creature, since it doesn't need a skeleton—just model-space geometry. I'm sketching rough dimensions, around 5.2m long, 2.2m wide, 1.9m tall, with the hover effect handled by positioning the lowest points above ground.

To avoid the vehicle looking like it's floating awkwardly, I decide to give it short landing skids that actually touch the floor, with the hover thruster pods tucked above them near the wheel arches. Then I block out the chassis layout—a frame, a cab up front, a hood, and a bed toward the rear—planning to build each section with simple flat-shaded boxes and a reusable helper function, finishing the body in a dark painted metal using the panelled styling from the clockwork kit.

Working out the body profile coordinates...

Still building window geometry...

For the design direction, I'm weighing military styling—roof turret, armor plating, roll cage, antenna, searchlight—against cyberpunk touches like neon pink/cyan accent strips and kanji decals, landing on a matte olive-black body with dark gunmetal accents.

Now I'm designing hover thrusters as four ducted-fan pods at the wheel positions, each built from a lathed shroud ring with a glowing cyan disc and fan blades inside, mounted via struts outside the body with skid legs underneath.

Writing duct geometry profile...

Positioning the thruster pack with housing between the nozzles, then moving to the front fascia with bull bar, glowing headlights, hazard-striped grille, and a light bar slab. I'm also planning door decals using SVG textures—unit numbers, chevrons, barcodes, hazard stripes—mapped onto planes on both sides of the vehicle.

Working out exact placement: the door emblem goes on the lower body side rather than the cab, positioned at the correct height and depth, with angular armor plates extruded over the side afterward for extra detail.

Now I'm planning the bed's turret mount with pedestal, gun body, barrel cylinders, ammo box, and shield, plus a roll cage of hoop and diagonal rods behind the cab, a neon glow bar on the roof, and antenna rods with glowing tips. I'm also sketching out the texture set, starting with a door texture combining a number and stripe pattern.

Beyond that I'm adding hazard stripes for the bumper and bed rim, a grille texture with glowing magenta slats, hood and tail decals, and a roof emblem — landing on around five or six textures total alongside body paint and metal materials. I'm settling on glow colors for cyan, magenta, and amber accents and starting a helper function to apply them consistently.

Writing box helper function...

Working out the bed walls, tailgate, and chassis dimensions, then placing a turret pedestal and gun mount toward the rear of the bed.

Now adding a roll cage with hoops, cargo crates with glowing cells, and flared side pods for a wide hover vehicle, checking that the pods don't overlap the lower body panels.

Placing skids at the floor and checking strut heights, then adding a glow disc under each pod for the fan effect along with a thin glow ring at the rim, plus six small blade boxes for the fan itself.

Now I'm shaping the front end: a bumper box, bull bar tubes, and glowing headlight bars positioned near the nose.

I'm working out grille placement along the sloped front face between the headlights, then moving to the rear with a tailgate tail-light texture, noting there are no wheel geometry details yet.

Next I'm planning the roof rack, a magenta glow light bar at the windshield top, a sensor dome with emblem, and rear roof-corner antenna rods with glowing tips, plus wing mirror boxes mounted on arms at the sides.

Now I'm adding thin neon underglow strips along the lower body sides (cyan) and pods (magenta), chevron armor plates on the hood, angular bed-side armor, and a shoulder spotlight, then moving to define the painted body material using a mottled, panelled texture with larger seam size and rivets for a weathered armored look.

Still writing materials and geometry...

Checking the roof gun doesn't clash with the lightbar placement, it clears fine. I'm also adding a rear missile pod in the bed: a tilted box housing a 2x3 grid of glowing-tipped tubes built as rods from base to tip positions, angled upward about 30 degrees for a militarized look.

Now I'm working out the cab glass glow color and double-checking the side window extrusion axis so the thickness runs correctly along x.

For the windshield, I'm computing the slanted slab geometry by finding the normal to the front cab edge line and offsetting points along it to get proper top and bottom coordinates for the glass panel.

I'll skip the fan texture and move on to composing the full model, treating decal textures as separate planes with a white base color so textures render true, and glowing only the non-door textured parts. For doors I'm designing an SVG texture with an orange stripe, "TX-07" text, small cyan glyph shapes, and hazard chevrons, sized to a 2:1 aspect plane positioned on the cab side.

Now I'm placing a hood emblem as a hexagon with a cyan eye on an upward-facing plane aligned to the sloped hood surface, lifted slightly to avoid z-fighting, then positioning a tail texture plane on the rear surface.

For the tail I'm adding red/magenta lights and a plate, applying a glow of 0.8 so the colors pop while darker regions stay subdued, and doing the same for the grille texture. I'm about to write the final code with a helper function to handle mirrored arrangements.
